newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Friday's Sri Lankan newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VEERAKESARI
At Mannar, the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) blast a telecommunications tower and a power station, killing two policemen and two soldiers, military officials say.
Student bodies organise strikes in the eastern Batticaloa region on Thursday to condemn the killing of eight Tamils last week by an unidentified group of gunmen. Shops, banks and offices were closed.
THINAKARAN
A group of 25 members of parliament will visit Ireland from October 13 to October 20 to study problems in Northern Ireland and learn ways to resolve Sri Lanka's ethnic problems.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte said on Thursday the government was not prepared to talk to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) unless the rebels accept the conditions laid down by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
DAILY NEWS
Sri Lanka to revamp railway services with help from Japan, Germany and Netherlands. The plan will cost 5.7 billion rupees.
The LTTE will have to first disarm completely if they want to enter into any peace talks, says deputy defence minister General Anuruddha Ratwatte.
THE ISLAND
Deputy defence minister says government is committed to destroying LTTE's military strength.
LANKADEEPA
LTTE destroys telecommunications tower and power station in Mannar in Mannar.
Colombo police arrest a man suspected of being a member of the LTTE's medical unit.
DINAMINA
The army will hunt and destroy the LTTE wherever it may base itself, says the deputy defence minister.
President Kumaratunga initiates plan to develop railways at a cost of 5.7 billion rupees.
DIVAINA
President Kumaratunga orders import of 800 buses using Indian credit line, as part of a plan to upgrade public transport.
--Colombo newsroom tel 941-434319
